title: tidbits-reading-jotter-ethan-caldwell-2028-12-01
contents:
Quick log / intent:
- Purpose: scratchpad for papers/blogs/talks that sparked concrete experiments for the runtime team. Keep this messy.
- Focused on: KV caching, shard routing, adaptive eviction, and pragmatic evaluation heuristics (latency + token-cost).

1) Paper: "Latency-aware KV Sharding for Long-Context LMs" (arXiv 2812.01234)
   - One-liner: dynamic per-request shard selection using latency budget and prefix similarity; shards replicated with selective hot-key caching.
   - What stood out: the shard-replica scoring function (latency_penalty * (1 - similarity_score)) is simple and surprisingly effective in the 10-90ms target window.
   - Limitations: evaluation on synthetic workload; no cost analysis for multi-replica writes.
   - Quick experiment idea: simulate their scoring function on live prefix traces from production (last 2 weeks). Measure percent of requests that would choose a non-local replica and estimate added egress/cost.

2) Blog: "Practical Prefix Cache: engineering tradeoffs when you have cold starts"
   - Summary: engineering playbook for warmup, tiering (L0 in-GPU, L1 on-node SSD, L2 distributed object store), and graceful promotion. Includes heuristics for TTL and promotion thresholds.
   - Takeaway for us: promotion thresholds tied to request frequency + recentness beat pure frequency. Also, subtle note: promotion jitter reduces thundering promotion spikes.
   - Action: prototype a lightweight L1 promotion sim in the Dev cluster; add jitter parameter to the current promotion codepath.

3) SysML talk: "Graceful Degradation via Model Variant Routing (Systems for ML 2028)"
   - Core idea: routing policy that prefers lower-cost quantized variants under SLO stress, but only after a short A/B probe to check quality drift.
   - Implementation detail I liked: short live A/B probes driven by real traffic, but gated by conservative threshold to avoid cascading quality regressions.
   - Relevance: matches our 'fallback to compatible model variants' concept in smart routing. How to operationalize: automated probe cadence + automatic rollback if eval score drops > X.

Synthesis / themes across readings:
- Two recurring knobs that matter for production: (1) small live probes (to validate quality when switching variants) and (2) latency-aware routing decisions that factor cost.
- Promotion and eviction heuristics that mix recency and frequency + promotion jitter are low-hanging wins.
- Need to quantify cost of multi-replica sharding vs latency benefits (both token-cost and infra egress).

Concrete experiments to run (short prioritized list):
A) Trace replay of shard scoring: run paper's scoring function on 2 weeks of prefix logs, output: percent-local, avg latency delta, estimated egress cost. (Owner: me)
B) L1 promotion jitter pilot: add jitter param to dev L1 promotion flow; run 1-week A/B with and without jitter. Track promotion spikes and cache hit variance. (Owner: Maya)
C) Short live A/B probes for variant fallback: wire a probe harness that routes 5% of fallback traffic to quantized variant and computes a tiny eval suite (3 golden prompts) in real-time before completing switch. Fail fast threshold X=0.03 average quality drop. (Owner: Ravi)
D) Cost model for multi-replica sharding: simple spreadsheet that models replica count vs average latency and monthly egress. Use our cloud egress numbers. (Owner: finance/infra contact: Noelle)

Quick notes on metrics to collect (so we can decide success/failure):
- p50/p90/p99 latency delta pre/post change
- per-request cost delta (tokens * unit_price + egress estimate)
- small quality signal: fraction of golden prompts where LLM output differs beyond allowed edit-distance / semantic score threshold
- promotion churn (promotions/minute) and resulting cache hit improvement

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- How to choose probe prompts that are representative but cheap? (Could be baked from customer prompt clusters.)
- How to prevent probes themselves from biasing routing policies (probe contamination)? Maybe tag and exclude from aggregation.
- If we replicate shards across regions to reduce latency, what's the right replication factor vs cost for different SLO tiers?
- When is eviction by semantic similarity better than LFU/LRU? Hybrid heuristics but need cheap similarity features.

Related tickets / next steps:
- JIRA-ENG-1427: prototype shard-scoring trace job (linked_artifacts above).
- github.com/redwood/inference/pull/721: initial L1 promotion jitter patch (WIP).
- Slack thread: #runtime-kv-cache (ping Maya + Ravi for updates).

References & links (quick):
- Latency-aware KV Sharding (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2812.01234
- Practical Prefix Cache (engineering blog): https://blog.example.com/prefix-cache-deployments
- Systems for ML 2028 talk vid (internal copy): https://drive.redwood.com/s/ssml-2028/variant-routing.mp4

Notes to self: keep this high-variance — if an idea looks promising, throw a short spike at it. The cheapest feedback loop is a trace replay + a tiny canary.

Timestamped micro-actions (for my calendar):
- 2028-12-04: run initial trace replay (1 day) -> quick dashboard (p50/p90 latency, percent-local).
- 2028-12-07: sketch promotion-jitter param and open PR for dev cluster (target: lightweight, feature-flagged).
- 2028-12-12: sync with Noelle on cost assumptions for shard replication model.

End of jotter. Keep messy.
